verdicts.reasoning: Both the sync banner and each integration health row use the system's Alert component, driven only by semantic intents ('success' | 'warning' | 'danger') through lookup maps. There are no hand-colored dots, no hex or rgb values, and no custom color CSS. Colors come from the component's intent handling. Partial deduction because Alert is a notification component rather than a dedicated status/label or badge component, and the API reference offers no such alternative to confirm one exists.

Every state carries text. Sync states show titles 'Sync online', 'Sync reconnecting', and 'Sync offline' with body copy. Integration health shows the visible labels 'Operational', 'Degraded', and 'Down' next to each integration name. Color is supplementary, not the only signal.

The diff sets no typography utility class or typography token on status text. The only typographic styling is the h2 heading, which sets margin and color only. Status text (the Alert titles and bodies, and the HEALTH_LABEL strings) is passed as plain children and props with no visible typography utility. Any typography comes from inside Alert, which the diff does not show, so the rubric item cannot be verified from the diff.
